text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola and grain futures pre-opening call as of 0840 CDT.

CANOLA - C$0.70 to C$1.20 a tonne higher on firmer CBOT soycomplex calls, expected local and commmercial short covering of the November due to hot, dry Prairie weather and today's forecast for the same. November WCE canola crush profit margins rose to -8.05 Tuesday vs -5.85 Friday. Canada's dollar opened lower at C$1.3835, rose to 86.29 yen and rose to 1.3623 marks.
FLAXSEED - Steady to C$1.00 down with November seen holding steady but September down on low cash markets.
Trade talk has soymeal stocks rising in Europe which curbed demand for Canadian flaxseed.
WESTERN BARLEY - C$0.40 to C$0.90 a tonne higher on CBOT corn calls and expected short covering.
FEED WHEAT - Steady, with more wheat expected to grade as feed, on news of widespread drought stress in western Manitoba and throughout Saskatchewan.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
